turns.assessment: The affected services all depend on lightpath och37, and both och37 line receivers recorded a single errored second while protected services switched away and restored after only 0.1 s. Unchanged power, OSNR, pre-FEC BER, DGD, amplifier, and pump measurements argue strongly against a persistent line-interface, WSS, amplifier, connector, or fibre-loss fault. A millisecond-scale SOP transient somewhere on the och37 fibre route best fits the brief bidirectional disturbance, but the evidence does not identify a specific span or other repairable element.

proposals.rationale: Fast polarization changes can cause errored seconds and short protection switches without a sampled optical-power change or persistent alarm. The simultaneous impact on services sharing och37 and the rapid recovery are characteristic, but no observation localizes the transient to one span.

A brief cable disturbance could create a sub-second power excursion affecting och37 and escape normal sampling. It is less likely because neither endpoint nor any in-line/channel power monitor recorded a change.

score.why: truth not in the reported set
